F:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Evaluates a 1-based postfix expression of three-valued logic by mapping P, Q, R, 0, 1, 2, +, -, and * into numeric codes in fit and then reducing the encoded array in place with AND, OR, and NOT operations." F]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> p </REF>: int "Value substituted for the variable token 'P' in the expression."
        <REF> q </REF>: int "Value substituted for the variable token 'Q' in the expression."
        <REF> r </REF>: int "Value substituted for the variable token 'R' in the expression."
        <REF> ft </REF>: char[100] "Character array holding the encoded expression; only indices 1 through fc-1 are scanned, so ft[0] is ignored."
        <REF> fc </REF>: int "Upper bound for the character scan; the mapping loop reads ft[ic] for ic from 1 to fc-1. After the scan, the sentinel/tail index used by the reduction loop is fc-1."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: int "Value stored in fit[1] after the in-place reduction of the encoded expression."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize every element of the local array fit[0] through fit[99] to 0. RESULT fit]
            [COMMAND Set ic to 1 as the starting index for scanning the expression in ft. RESULT ic]
            [COMMAND While ic is less than fc, map the character at ft[ic] to fit[ic] as follows: 'P' to p, 'Q' to q, 'R' to r, '0' to 0, '1' to 1, '2' to 2, '+' to 3, '-' to 4, and '*' to 5; for any other character, leave fit[ic] as its initialized value 0; then increment ic by 1. RESULT fit_mapped]
            [COMMAND Decrement ic by 1, so ic becomes fc-1, the sentinel/tail index that is not scanned as an operator cursor in the reduction loop. RESULT ic]
            [COMMAND Set x to 1 as the starting cursor for the reduction loop. RESULT x]
            [COMMAND While x is less than ic, perform the in-place postfix reduction of fit, processing each cursor position x from 1 through ic-1. RESULT fit_reduced]
            [COMMAND Within the reduction loop, evaluate the if conditions for fit[x] equal to 3, 4, and 5 as independent sequential conditions; do not treat them as an if/else-if chain, so a later condition may use the updated cursor and array from an earlier match in the same iteration. RESULT fit_reduced]
            [COMMAND Within the reduction loop, if fit[x] equals 3, treat it as three-valued OR: using short-circuit condition checks, if fit[x-1] is 0 and fit[x-2] is 0 then store 0 at fit[x-2]; otherwise if either fit[x-1] or fit[x-2] is 2 then store 2 at fit[x-2]; otherwise store 1 at fit[x-2]. Then decrement ic by 2, shift fit[x-1] through fit[ic] left by 2 positions, and decrement x by 2 so that the final loop increment leaves the cursor one position before the original x. RESULT fit_reduced]
            [COMMAND Within the reduction loop, if fit[x] equals 4, treat it as three-valued NOT: assign fit[x-1] the value 2 - fit[x-1]. Then decrement ic by 1, shift fit[x] through fit[ic] left by 1 position, and decrement x by 1 so that the final loop increment leaves the cursor at the same effective position. RESULT fit_reduced]
            [COMMAND Within the reduction loop, if fit[x] equals 5, treat it as three-valued AND: using short-circuit condition checks, if either fit[x-1] or fit[x-2] is 0 then store 0 at fit[x-2]; otherwise if both fit[x-1] and fit[x-2] are 2 then store 2 at fit[x-2]; otherwise store 1 at fit[x-2]. Then decrement ic by 2, shift fit[x-1] through fit[ic] left by 2 positions, and decrement x by 2 so that the final loop increment leaves the cursor one position before the original x. RESULT fit_reduced]
            [COMMAND After the three independent if checks for values 3, 4, and 5 have been evaluated sequentially in the current iteration, increment x by 1 and continue the while loop. RESULT x]
            [COMMAND Return the value at fit[1] as the result of the expression evaluation. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
